questiontext.text:
An angle \(\theta\) is given in radians as: \(\theta={@angle_rad@}\text{ radians}.\)

Convert the given angle from radians to degrees.

Show your answer in degrees.

[[input:ans1]] °

[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We are given the angle:

\(\theta={@angle_rad@}\text{ radians}.\)

Step 1: Recall the conversion relationship

We know that:

\(\pi\text{ radians}=180^\circ.\)

Therefore, to convert an angle from radians to degrees, we multiply by \(\frac{180^\circ}{\pi}\).

Step 2: Apply the conversion formula

\(\theta_{\text{degrees}}=\theta_{\text{radians}}\times\frac{180^\circ}{\pi}\).

Substitute the given angle:

\(\theta_{\text{degrees}}=\frac{@k@\pi}{6}\times\frac{180^\circ}{\pi}\).

Step 3: Simplify

Cancel \(\pi\) from the numerator and denominator:

\(\theta_{\text{degrees}}=\frac{@k@\times180^\circ}{6}\).

Therefore:

\(\theta_{\text{degrees}}={@ta@}^\circ\).

Final Answer

The equivalent angle in degrees is:

\(\boxed{{@ta@}^\circ}\).

Key concept: To convert radians to degrees, multiply the angle in radians by \(\frac{180^\circ}{\pi}\).
